steps: RefineQueue.mjs: find owner prompts, queue, run Haiku, write refined cards (40 min)
review 10 products vs raw, tune the brief, rerun (30 min)
docs-check, review.mjs, four widths, merge, land (30 min)

decision.what: Owner prompts = typed/dictated user turns in VS Code (entrypoint claude-vscode) transcripts, minus relays ([from: …], [You are …]) and compaction summaries; each prompt referenced as <session>:<transcript line>.
decision.alternative: the Echo Prompt items in session page.jsonl (none since 10-09, and 10-08's 423 'owner' items are mislabeled agent prompts) or prompt-relay's .claude/prompts (stopped 10-02)

decision.what: The Haiku 'minion' is one Agent-SDK query() per prompt with no tools (askOnce), started by node, not a Servex agent: lean context, no Servex queue, node starts the next.
decision.alternative: spawn_agent per prompt (a full agent context and Servex's spawn gate for a one-call job)

decision.what: Refined cards go into each session's own page.jsonl through page_tools' own page_add handler (imported in node); that file is gitignored (local, beside the raw transcript it cites), so a compact committed asks.jsonl (one line per ask) in this task dir is the committed record and feeds --repeats.
decision.alternative: commit the full cards (copies near-verbatim owner text into git)

experiment.try: lean RefineCall (no tools, no MCP, settingSources []) run with cwd = repo vs cwd = os.tmpdir()
experiment.measure: tokens and $ for a 'Say hi' call on Haiku
experiment.result: repo cwd: 8,203 cache-write tokens, $0.066; temp cwd: 406 tokens, $0.0018. The 8k is the project's auto-memory (MEMORY.md), loaded whatever settingSources says. RefineCall gets an opt-in cwd; RefineQueue uses it.

log.msg: v1 run on 10 prompts: $1.747 (0.175/prompt, before the cwd fix), max 30,785 tokens a call, 177 asks. Opus review of v1: coverage 0.97, 0.94, 0.91, 0.96, 1.0, 0.5, 0.88, 1.0, 0.83, 1.0 = mean 0.90 (score = faithful asks / (true asks + invented asks); confidence 0.7 each). Failure modes: narration turned into asks, a self-correction ignored, a pushback read as the idea, a referent misread. v2 brief = specifics first + four rules for those.
log.now: v2 rerun of the same 10 in background; building the Coverage tab

decision.what: Merge once at the end (merge.mjs refuses a full-size branch without a review), so the v2 rerun still pays the pre-fix cost (~$1.75).
decision.alternative: review + merge the queue slice alone first (a second review pass, more than the $1.60 it would save)

experiment.try: brief v2 (specifics first + 4 rules from the v1 review) on the same 10 prompts
experiment.measure: Opus coverage score, mean of 10 (faithful / (true + invented asks))
experiment.result: v1 0.90 -> v2 0.96; worst v1 0.5 -> v2 0.8 (narration still read as an ask once). v2 kept. review.md

log.msg: Coverage tab built (AISessionCoverage.js) and drawn in the worktree; verdicts match asks-outcomes by prompt then by feature name, fetched only when files.jsonl lists it
log.now: docs + promotion rule + --repeats, then docs-check and review
